TL;DR
We're looking for an exceptional AI Software Engineer to build the AI-powered People systems that help Lovable scale.
As Lovable grows, we're rethinking how work gets done. Rather than relying on traditional HR software, we're building AI-native products that transform hiring, onboarding, workforce planning, identity, compliance, and other core People workflows.
You'll work embedded with our People team, partnering closely with stakeholders to understand problems, design solutions, and ship production-ready software. Many of the products you build won't stop at improving Lovable internally — they have the potential to become capabilities we offer to customers in the future, giving you the opportunity to shape products that start inside Lovable and scale far beyond it.
Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
Why join now?
Very few engineering roles offer this level of ownership.
You'll help define how AI transforms internal operations. You'll work directly with the People team to identify problems, design solutions, and build products that improve how Lovable operates every day.
As Lovable scales, we're building the operating system the company runs on—function by function, directly in Lovable. The People team is one of the first. You'll help define how AI transforms one of our most important internal functions, and the best ideas will eventually become building blocks for our customers.
What we're looking for
We're looking for a software engineer with strong product instincts and experience building secure software that handles sensitive information.
You'll likely have:
Experience shipping production software that handles sensitive data — HR tech, fintech, identity management, or similar.
Experience working with people data, business systems, analytics platforms, or enterprise data infrastructure (e.g. BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, Airflow, Fivetran, SQL, etc.).
Deep familiarity with HR systems and/or ATS platforms (HiBob, Ashby, Workday, Greenhouse, or similar), either as a builder or through close collaboration with People teams.
Experience designing secure systems with role-based access control and data permissioning.
Strong product instincts—you think end-to-end, ask why, and care about building products people actually use.
Excellent stakeholder management skills and the ability to translate operational challenges into technical solutions.
Experience building products from scratch and taking them into production.

Bonus points if you have:
Experience at an HR technology company, Work OS platform, or identity provider,
Experience with HRIS, ATS, compensation, workforce planning tools.
Experience building AI-powered products or internal tooling.
Experience working closely with People or Operations teams.

What you'll do
In one sentence:
Build AI-powered People systems that make Lovable run better — and create products that can graduate from internal tools to customer-facing features.
Examples include:
Partner with the People team to identify, scope, and ship AI-powered internal products.
Build integrations with HR systems (HiBob, Ashby, etc.), ATS platforms, and identity providers.
Design secure systems with robust role-based permissions and access controls.
Develop predictive and diagnostic models (workforce trends, hiring capacity, retention risks, compensation dynamics).
Create canonical datasets and source-of-truth models for hiring, headcount, compensation, organizational design, and workforce planning.
Data governance — source-of-truth logic, naming conventions, ownership.
Own products end-to-end—from research and design through implementation, deployment, and iteration.
Translate operational challenges into elegant technical solutions.
Build systems that meet legal and compliance requirements for handling sensitive employee data.
Work closely with other AI Ops Engineers, sharing building blocks, patterns, and learnings across Lovable's functions.
Build AI agents, workflows, dashboards, and decision-support tools that help leaders make better decisions.

Our tech stack
We're building with tools that both humans and AI love.
Languages: TypeScript, Python, Go
AI: OpenAI, Anthropic, MCP, AI Agents
Business Systems: HiBob, Ashby, Okta
Infrastructure: Cloudflare, PostgreSQL, Temporal
We're always looking for better tools and better ways of building software.
About your application
Please submit your application in English — it's our company language.
We review every application carefully and encourage anyone excited by the role to apply, even if your background doesn't perfectly match every bullet point.

jobs.occupation: Electronics System Engineer to Beyond Gravity Gothenburg
jobs.description:
🚀 Challenge the Impossible​ ​
 
About Beyond Gravity
Beyond Gravity, headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, is the first space company to combine a startup mindset, agility, speed and innovation with decades of experience and proven quality. Approximately 1800 employees at 12 locations in six countries (Switzerland, Sweden, Austria, USA, Finland and Portugal) develop and manufacture products for satellites and launch vehicles with the goal of advancing humankind and enabling the exploration of the world and beyond. Beyond Gravity is the preferred supplier of structures for all types of launch vehicles and a leading provider of selected satellite products and constellation solutions in the New Space sector. In 2024, the company generated a revenue of around CHF 359 million. More information at: www.beyondgravity.com
 
Your crew

Join a highly collaborative, cross-functional team at the heart of Beyond Gravity’s Electronics business. Working closely with Engineering, Product Management, Programs, Production and other functions, you will contribute to the development of satellite onboard systems, platform and payload products as well as ground electronics products.
As an Electronics System Engineer, you will work at system and architectural level, providing system engineering expertise for electronics hardware systems, embedded processing systems and platform and payload solutions across development projects and series production programs in the satellite electronic solutions domain.
This is a role with significant development potential. You will have the opportunity to take increasing ownership, broaden your technical expertise and grow towards more advanced system engineering responsibilities over time.
 
Your mission

The Electronics System Engineer is responsible for:
Take ownership of your scope and bring assigned tasks to completion, involving more senior colleagues when needed.
Develop and maintain satellite onboard systems, platform and payload products as well as ground electronics products at system and architectural level.
Analyse and understand internal and external customer requirements and translate them into system-level requirements and technical solutions.
Break down system requirements into subsystem and module requirements and establish corresponding design requirements.
Develop technical concepts and system designs appropriate to customer and project needs, considering cost, time, quality, performance and technical feasibility.
Perform and/or assess system-level analyses, including performance, radiation, structural, EMC, reliability, FDIR and HW/FPGA/SW interaction analyses.
Coordinate development activities with other teams and disciplines to ensure complete and intended implementation of the system.
Plan and execute your own activities, monitor progress against schedule and budget, and raise awareness of risks and blocking points.
Support bidding and proposal activities through technical descriptions, concept work, cost and schedule estimates and risk and opportunity assessments.
Contribute to continuous improvement of products, technologies, processes and ways of working, challenging established solutions where appropriate.
Interact with customers, suppliers and external stakeholders within your area of responsibility and provide technical know-how to support successful project execution.
Maintain and develop system-level documentation and ensure compliance with established development processes and standards.

 
Most important outputs:
Robust and efficient system solutions that meet customer and project requirements.
Successful delivery of system engineering activities within agreed scope, quality, schedule and budget.
Continuous development of products, technologies and engineering methods.

 
Your story

We are looking for a technically curious and solution-oriented System Engineer with a strong interest in satellite electronics and system engineering. You take ownership of your work, are comfortable working independently and enjoy finding solutions to complex technical challenges.
You have a collaborative mindset and enjoy working across disciplines, with the ability to communicate clearly with colleagues, customers and external partners. You are motivated by continuous learning and want to develop your expertise and responsibility over time.
This role is a great opportunity for someone with strong potential to grow towards more advanced system engineering responsibilities and, in time, a Senior System Engineer role.
 
Must-haves:
M.Sc. in Electrical, Software or Aerospace Engineering, or corresponding experience.
Experience or good knowledge in system engineering, electronics or embedded systems, preferably within the space industry.
Understanding of requirements engineering, functional decomposition and system design.
Ability to perform or assess system-level analyses and understand HW/FPGA/SW interactions.
Ability to work independently, take ownership and deliver within agreed scope, schedule and budget.
Strong collaboration and communication skills.
Structured and solution-oriented approach to technical challenges and risk.
Fluent English, written and spoken.

 
Nice to have’s:
Experience with satellite onboard systems, platform and payload products or ground electronics.
Knowledge of FPGA, hardware, RF, signal processing or embedded systems.
Experience with tools such as MATLAB, DOORS, PSA, FMECA, DOSRAD or Reliability.
Knowledge of ECSS, agile methods or model-based systems engineering.
Experience with technical coordination, customer interaction or proposal work.
Knowledge of product roadmaps and current technology trends.

 
Why Beyond Gravity
 
To work in a growing high technology company with career opportunities within the site or internationally.
You will be a part of an engaged team with the ambition to innovate space!
We offer a hybrid work situation, high flexibility and autonomy, and a great team to develop and have fun with!

 
🌌Are you ready for lift-off?​
Our core values - Passionate, Together, and Curious - transform challenges into opportunities. Embark on a journey to transcend the ordinary with us. We‘re actively reviewing candidates and will promptly select the ideal fit for our team.​
​Beyond Gravity is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

At UMS Skeldar, you get the unique chance to leave your footprint within our organization with fast reaction times and high engagement.

Join our Flight Operations team as a UAS Flight Manager and take a key role in leading and developing our growing flight organization. You will lead our flight operations, develop our flight crews and ways of working, and play an important part in shaping the future of unmanned aviation. The role is both operational and strategic. You will be close to the daily flight operations while also developing our people, processes, and ways of working as our UAS operations continue to grow. You will report to the Head of Flight Operations.

Act as a key point of contact for operation sites, aviation authorities, customers, and internal stakeholders, supporting customer deliveries, demonstrations, new operational concepts, and other flight activities.

Bring the Future of Wind Propulsion Onboard

About Us
Wind helped us discover our planet, and now it can help us preserve it. Our vision is to provide wings for a shipping revolution, and we have two strong mother companies to back us up: Alfa Laval and Wallenius.
Would you like to contribute to this change, then join our fast-growing, highly competent and passionate team. AlfaWall Oceanbird AB is a 50/50 joint venture, owned by Alfa Laval and Wallenius but operated as an independent company. We are developing wing sail technology for the global shipping market and are now looking for an Installation Lead to join our team. Help us bring wind propulsion from shore to ship!
The role
As Oceanbird moves from a prototype stage into commercial customer delivery, successful installation is becoming one of our most important capabilities.
As Installation Lead, you will turn plans and technical solutions into safe, efficient and wellcoordinated installations at shipyards and onboard vessels. You will also be responsible for our demonstrator wing in Landskrona, coordinating its operation, maintenance and test readiness so that it provides the data needed for our continued development.

You will be part of the Project Management Office and work closely with our project managers. During installations, you will lead a cross-functional team of approximately 3–8 people, including electricians, service engineers, technical specialists and external contractors.
The Project Manager retains overall responsibility for the customer project, while you lead the dayto-day installation activities and safe execution at the shipyard, in harbor or at sea.

Your main responsibilities:
• Plan, prepare and lead installation and commissioning activities at shipyards/harbour and onboard vessels.
• Translate project and engineering requirements into practical installation plans, work sequences, resource needs and schedules.
• Coordinate the on-site installation team and act as Oceanbird’s operational interface with shipyards, vessel crews, customers and subcontractors.
• Lead the safe execution of installation work, ensuring that risk assessments, work permits, toolbox talks and agreed safety procedures are in place and followed.
• Monitor progress, quality and safety, resolve practical issues and escalate risks or decisions when required.
• Develop and maintain installation procedures, method statements, SOPs, checklists and installation manuals.
• Capture lessons learned and use them to improve future installations, documentation and ways of working.
• Coordinate the operation, maintenance, inspection and test readiness of the demonstrator wing and its supporting equipment in Landskrona.
• Plan activities together with the Landskrona team and work closely with our teams in Flemingsberg to incorporate experience from installations and testing into our continued development.

Who are you?
You are a practical and confident installation leader who can bring people from different disciplines together, create structure and maintain focus on safety and delivery—even when conditions change.
You are likely to have:
• Experience leading installations, commissioning, service or major maintenance involving complex mechanical or electromechanical equipment.

Classified by Alfa Laval as: Business
• Experience from commercial vessels and shipyards, ideally involving bulk carriers, tankers or similar vessel types.
• Experience from newbuild projects and working closely with shipyards in Asia is highly valuable.
• A relevant engineering qualification within mechanical, marine, electrical or a related technical field. This could be a vocational, college or bachelor-level qualification, or equivalent experience.
• A strong understanding of safe working practices in shipyard, industrial or onboard environments.
• Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams, contractors and external stakeholders.
• The ability to produce clear and practical technical documentation, including SOPs and installation manuals.
• Professional proficiency in English and the willingness to travel internationally and work onboard vessels.

You are safety-conscious, structured and calm under pressure. You communicate clearly across technical disciplines and cultures and are comfortable moving between planning, documentation and hands-on execution.

Location and travel
We are open to discussing the location for the right candidate, although proximity to either Flemingsberg or Landskrona is preferred.
Regular international travel and periods of work at shipyards and onboard vessels are an integral part of the role.

What we offer
At Oceanbird, you will help turn a bold vision into working technology at sea. You will see the direct result of your work as our wing sail technology moves from development and testing to installation onboard commercial vessels—and ultimately into operation at sea.
This is an opportunity to shape not only how our first commercial installations are delivered, but how Oceanbird will install wing sails around the world in the future. Working alongside highly skilled and passionate colleagues, you will influence our installation methods, safety standards and ways of working—and contribute directly to making wind a powerful part of cleaner shipping.

Join us in redefining the future of clean shipping.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in materials informatics and materials digital infrastructure
jobs.description:
Work assignments 
The primary focus of the position is on developing methods and software for making materials data accessible, interoperable, and reusable, as well as for managing, processing, and analyzing large-scale materials datasets. The research aims to advance data-driven materials science by improving the standardization, exchange, and utilization of research data and computational tools.
 
The work may include the development of methods for data management and interoperability, standardized data representations, integration of databases and computational workflows, and the application of AI/machine learning methods to materials data. The research may also involve the development and application of computational physics methods, high-throughput simulations, and data-driven approaches to understanding and predicting materials properties.
 
The position is connected to the EU project MaterialsCommons, which aims to establish a federated European digital infrastructure and a common digital market for materials data and services, connecting databases, computational tools, and other digital resources across institutions and national boundaries.
As postdoc, you will principally carry out research. A certain amount of teaching may be part of your duties, up to a maximum of 20% of working hours.
Qualifications
To be qualified to take employment as postdoc, you must have been awarded a doctoral degree or have a foreign degree that is deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree.  This degree must have been awarded at the latest by the point at which LiU makes its decision to employ you.
It is considered advantageous if your doctoral degree is no older than three years at application deadline for this job. If there are special reasons for having an older doctoral degree – such as taking statutory leave – then these may be taken into consideration.
Your application must include documents that clearly show that you fulfill the following requirements for the position:
A doctoral degree in physics, materials science, or equivalent. A course transcript with grades must be included in the application.
A record of multiple research publications in theoretical and computational materials science, materials design, and/or materials informatics.
Co-authored publications demonstrating experience with data-driven materials research.
Extensive, documented programming experience, particularly in Python, demonstrated, for example, through co-authored publications describing the use of Python and links to open-source software to which the applicant has contributed.

It is considered a strong merit for the position if your application shows (i) co-authored publications that involve work with materials databases and datasets; (ii) direct technical experience with maintaining materials databases and making research data accessible through them.
It is considered a merit for the position if your application shows: (i) course transcripts demonstrating high grades in completed courses of high relevance to the work assignments; (ii) other documented experience demonstrating a high level of understanding and skill in the fields of thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, group theory, crystallography, and crystal symmetry; (iii) experience with AI/ML for materials science.
You are expected to be creative, independent, and intellectually curious, and to have a high level of engagement and motivation to contribute to materials science and materials data infrastructure.
The workplace
The position is at the Materials Design and Informatics Unit within the Division of Theoretical Physics, Department of Physics, Chemistry and Biology (IFM), Linköping University.
The unit conducts research in theoretical and computational physics, with a particular emphasis on computational materials science and materials informatics. Our research includes large-scale computational studies of materials, development of software and automated workflows for scientific computations, management and analysis of data in large-scale materials databases, and development and application of informatics, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning (ML) methods in materials science.
More information at: https://liu.se/en/research/materials-design-and-informatics
The employment
This employment is a temporary contract of two years with the possibility of extension up to a total maximum of three years.
 
The employment is full-time.
Starting date by agreement.
Salary and employment benefits
At Linköping University, salaries are set individually and differentiated, in accordance with the applicable collective agreements (RALS/RALS-T) and the university’s salary-setting guidelines.
More information about employee benefits is available https://liu.se/en/work-at-liu/employee-benefits.
Union representatives
Information about union representatives, see https://liu.se/en/work-at-liu/hjalp%20for%20sokande.
Application procedure
Apply for the position by clicking the “Apply” button. Your application must be received no later than 8 December, 2026. 
 
 
 
Applications and documents received after the date above will not be considered. 
 
 
 
Please attach your selected research publications electronically, in pdf or word format, in the application template. Research publications, e.g. monographs, which cannot be sent electronically should be sent in three sets by mail to the University Registrar at Linköping University, University Registrar, S-581 83 Linköping, Sweden. The publications must be received by Linköping University no later than the deadline for application. 
Please note that printed publications will not be returned. They will be archived at Linköping University. 
 
 
 
In the event of a discrepancy between the English translation of the job announcement and the Swedish original, the Swedish version shall take precedent. 
 
We welcome applicants with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives - diversity enriches our work and helps us grow. Preserving everybody's equal value, rights and opportunities is a natural part of who we are. Read more about our work with: https://liu.se/en/article/lika-villkor/.
 
 
We look forward to receiving your application!

jobs.occupation: Development Engineer within R&D to Olink
jobs.description:
Would you like to work hands-on with laboratory development and contribute to the next generation of Life Science products? At Olink, you will have the opportunity to be part of developing innovative protein biomarker panels that help researchers worldwide better understand complex diseases and advance the field of precision medicine. As a Development Engineer, you will combine practical laboratory work with method development, experimental evaluation, and the optimization of advanced workflows. We are looking for someone with experience in laboratory work within areas such as molecular biology, biotechnology, or assay development, who enjoys working hands-on in a laboratory environment and is motivated by turning scientific concepts into products that can make a real difference to human health. We look forward to receiving your application!
About the role
Olink – Part of Thermo Fisher Scientific has experienced tremendous growth in recent years and has quickly made a global impact. Its groundbreaking products are used by leading research institutes and pharmaceutical companies to drive the next major breakthroughs in medicine. With headquarters and service laboratories in both Uppsala and Boston, Olink is a truly global Life Science company. Its technology is developed and used to provide new insights into complex diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular diseases, and neurological disorders – research that has the potential to genuinely change people's lives.
Olink is now looking for a Development Engineer to join its R&D team, Reveal Development, which is responsible for developing a specific product line within mid-plex solutions. The team focuses on developing and evaluating new protein panels, assessing their performance, and optimizing the laboratory processes used in product development. In this role, you will contribute to hands-on development activities, conducting experiments and laboratory testing to help ensure that new panels and methods meet established requirements.
The role is primarily hands-on and laboratory-based. Your responsibilities will include conducting experiments, performing pipetting, operating laboratory instruments, and working with automated processes. An important part of the role will also involve evaluating and documenting test results and identifying opportunities to improve existing methods and workflows. You will work according to project plans and maintain close communication with project leads regarding the planning, prioritization, and execution of different tests.
You will join a team of approximately 10 people, consisting of Development Engineers and Scientists. The team has a relatively new structure and is still evolving, but already offers a positive working environment where colleagues support one another and share knowledge. You will work closely with your team members while also collaborating with other functions across the organization. Your onboarding will include practical training, a structured onboarding checklist, and a dedicated mentor to support you during your initial period.
This is a consultant assignment, meaning you will be employed by Academic Work and work on-site at Olink. The assignment will initially run for six months, with the possibility of an extension. The planned start date is February or March 2027. The role is primarily based on-site in the laboratory in Uppsala, with some flexibility to work remotely when the tasks allow.
You are offered
The opportunity to work with innovative proteomics technology at an international Life Science company
A hands-on and rewarding role where you will contribute to the development of next-generation protein biomarker panels
The opportunity to combine laboratory work with method development, optimization, and automated processes
An important role within an R&D team, where your work directly contributes to the development of new products
A collaborative team of Development Engineers and Scientists, where knowledge sharing and mutual support are part of everyday work
A structured onboarding process, including a dedicated mentor and practical training
A workplace that our current consultants describe as fantastic

Work tasks
In this role, you will primarily work hands-on in the laboratory with the experimental development and evaluation of new protein biomarker panels. You will collaborate closely with project leads and other team members to plan, conduct, and follow up on experiments. Your responsibilities will include:
Planning and conducting laboratory experiments in accordance with project plans and established timelines
Performing laboratory work, including pipetting and other molecular biology techniques
Evaluating the performance of assays and new protein biomarker panels using established analytical tools and quality criteria
Analyzing, documenting, and communicating experimental results in accordance with established procedures
Working with automated laboratory processes, including operating and setting up laboratory instruments
Contributing to the optimization and further development of laboratory methods and workflows
Collaborating with project leads on the planning, prioritization, and execution of project activities
Participating in technical discussions, troubleshooting activities, and scientific reviews
Collaborating cross-functionally with other R&D teams to support product development milestones

We are looking for someone who
Holds a university degree in Molecular Biology, Biotechnology, Biochemistry, or another relevant scientific discipline
Has experience in laboratory work within areas such as assay development, product development, or research-based laboratory environments
Has hands-on experience with molecular biology techniques such as PCR, qPCR, NGS library preparation, and/or immunoassays
Has experience analyzing and interpreting experimental data and drawing scientifically sound conclusions
Has strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to document and communicate results effectively
Has good knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

It is considered an advantage, but not a requirement, if you have
Experience with multiplex protein detection technologies or molecular diagnostics platforms
Experience working with laboratory automation systems and high-throughput workflows
Experience with LIMS and structured experimental doc

Department Manager for Land Use and Community Relations
Boliden is a high-tech metals company with its own mines and smelters that works long-term to guarantee society's access to base and precious metals. For a century, our work has been part of the value chains that have shaped modern society. At Boliden, we know that the metals we mine and make available will continue to play a crucial role in the future – what matters is how we produce them. Become a part of us and drive change for generations to come.
Your opportunity 
Lead the stewardship of Boliden Mines’ land and forest holdings and secure the land our mines need to operate and develop over the long term. Boliden’s holdings include approximately 17,000 hectares of forest land, providing a substantial platform for long-term forest management and biodiversity initiatives.
As Head of Land & Forest, you will lead and develop a specialist team whose work spans forest management and harvesting, land acquisition and sales, biodiversity, community relations and geographic information systems (GIS). You will work with Boliden Mines business units and sites, landowners, public authorities, Sámi communities and other local stakeholders to build the relationships that underpin our social licence to operate.
You will set priorities for how Boliden manages its forests and plans for future land needs. That means weighing the long-term value of our forest holdings alongside operational needs, biodiversity and competing uses of land. 
Who you will work with
You will lead and support a geographically diverse team of seven specialists based in Boliden, Gällivare, and Stockholm, including three Forest & Land Coordinators, two Social Sustainability Coordinators, one GIS Strategist, and one Biodiversity Specialist.
You will also collaborate with internal teams, business units, landowners, public authorities, consultants and community stakeholders. You will also coordinate work across sites and represent Boliden in external forums where land, biodiversity and community matters are discussed.
The position is placed in Boliden, you report to the Director of Sustainability for Boliden Mines 
What you will do 
Your main responsibilities include:
Lead Boliden Mines’ work to secure the land our mines need to operate and develop. Work with the sites to identify future land needs early and translate them into plans, priorities and agreements.
Ensure staffing, competence development, and health, safety and environmental matters within the team.
Set the direction for managing approximately 17,000 hectares of forest land and the wider land and property portfolio. Use financial and operational analysis to weigh the costs, risks and long-term value of different options, from land acquisition and use to forestry and divestment.
Translate Boliden’s biodiversity commitments into practical priorities for forest management and land-use planning, working with your team and the mine sites.

What you bring 
You have led and developed specialist teams and bring substantial experience in forest management. You have made decisions that balance operational, commercial and environmental priorities, and you know how to turn long-term plans into work your team can deliver.
A degree in forestry, such as a Swedish Jägmästarexamen or Skogsmästarexamen, or equivalent expertise gained through substantial relevant experience.
Experience in long-term forest planning and operational forestry, with the ability to assess the financial implications of land and forest management decisions.
Experience negotiating agreements with landowners or other external parties and building trust where land-use interests differ.
A leadership style that gives specialists clear direction, supports their development and helps them work across disciplines and sites.
Proficiency in Swedish and English and a valid EU Category B driving licence.

Experience in strategic land access, land transactions, dialogue with Sámi communities or a land-intensive industry such as mining, energy or infrastructure is an advantage.
Why work with us
At Boliden, we believe in promoting a workplace where care, courage, and responsibility are central to everything we do. We offer a workplace where we believe in collaboration and where what you contribute will have a direct impact on future generations. We are a company made up of responsible and creative people all working towards the same vision; to become the most sustainable and respected metal supplier in the world. 
Apply today to be part of something truly meaningful! 
At Boliden, diversity and inclusion are drivers of innovation. We know that different perspectives and experiences strengthen us and help us stay at the forefront of an important and exciting industry. Therefore, we encourage applications from people with diverse backgrounds and viewpoints. Together, we have built a workplace where everyone can feel safe and inspired to reach their full potential.

jobs.occupation: Engineering Manager - Video Analytics, Sophia Antipolis
jobs.description:
Axis is hiring an Engineering Manager on the French Riviera, where the Alps meet the sea!
Lead our Sophia-Antipolis video analytics team and help shape the future of AI-based analytics running on millions of cameras worldwide.
Do you get your energy from developing people and helping a team deliver? Do you want to work with cutting-edge AI where you have real influence on product direction? As Engineering Manager - Video Analytics, you will make sure our engineers have the support, structure and coaching they need to build products that matter.

Who is your future team?

We are an international team of around 15 computer vision and graphics, AI and software engineers in Sophia-Antipolis. Today the team is organized into sub-teams that form around the features and products we build. We also work hand in hand with a dedicated QA team based on the same site. Together we cover the full chain of video analytics: research, data, algorithm and product development, accuracy evaluation and quality assurance to deliver and maintain market-ready products. We work closely with the other analytics teams across Axis R&D sites as well as other software, hardware and product management teams.
Our secret? Passion, kindness and knowledge sharing, all in a great place to live and work.
What you'll do here as Engineering Manager?
You will lead the team and report to the Site Manager. This is a hands-on role: beyond people management, you will do project management work and own how the team plans and delivers - backlog, priorities, project coordination, and the path from innovation work to product. As AI changes the way software is built, this role will evolve too: you will help define what engineering management looks like in an AI-augmented team, and how planning, delivery and people development adapt.
Your main tasks will be to:
Lead, inspire and develop your engineers, balancing the needs of the company with the needs of each individual.
Own planning and the backlog: set priorities with engineering and product stakeholders, and work with tech leads, QA and product owners.
Be accountable for delivery: make sure the team meets its commitments and that progress is visible to stakeholders.
Drive continuous improvement of how the team works: processes, AI-enabled tools and engineering practices.
Support and improve how the team is organized: provide operational support to the sub-teams and their leads and adapt our setup as features and products evolve.
Turn innovation into product: ensure research initiatives are clearly scoped and followed up, and that the most promising ones make it efficiently into product features.
Contribute to the technical and strategic direction of our analytics area, together with the Analytics management team.
Collaborate across sites, especially with R&D and product management in Sweden, and with business stakeholders.
Build the right competences through recruitment and onboarding, so the team has the skills our roadmap needs.
Handle standard management tasks: development talks, salary reviews and team budget.

Who are we looking for?

You have a strong technical interest and enjoy driving strategic and technical initiatives. You lead from a people perspective. You create a safe environment for coaching, feedback and collaboration, and you know how to combine listening with deciding. You challenge engineers constructively, help them prioritize, make clear trade-offs and keep the team focused on what matters most. You are comfortable working across sites and cultures, and you are curious about how AI is changing the way software products are built.
We're looking for someone who embodies Axis' values - openness, teamwork and collaboration - and who enjoys turning ideas into structured, high-impact results in a dynamic R&D environment.
We'd love to hear that you have/are:
A master's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or a related engineering field - a focus on imaging or video is a plus.
Proven experience leading software engineers, as project manager, team lead or engineering manager.
Experience working in an Agile setup, including backlog ownership and delivery planning, with strong project management skills and good knowledge of common methods and tools (e.g., Scrum, Kanban, Jira, Confluence).
A solid software development background and a strong track record of building and shipping high-quality software products.
A collaborative mindset and the ability to foster team spirit.
A structured and pragmatic way of working, strong communication skills and a long-term view of the full product lifecycle.
Fluent English and French, both required for daily collaboration and cross-site work (Swedish is a plus).

Bonus points for experience in:
Embedded software or camera/imaging systems.
Video analytics, computer vision or deep learning algorithm development.
Software architecture and tooling that improve team productivity.

What Axis has to offer

Join a global leader in network video and work with modern technologies alongside highly skilled colleagues around the world. You will have real room to shape the team, its ways of working and its products.
This is an on-site role at our Sophia-Antipolis office. As part of the team there, you'll enjoy a caring environment, sustainable mobility incentives, a corporate bonus, ongoing training and self-development, comprehensive insurance and a pension plan, plus additional local perks. You'll also collaborate closely with our teams in Sweden, with opportunities to travel for onboarding, management forums and joint projects.

jobs.occupation: Platform Engineer, Observability at Husqvarna Group
jobs.description:
Do you want to help developers understand how their software behaves in production, working side by side with them?

Our mission is to enable our DevOps teams to focus on building great applications by providing a shared internal developer platform, tools, templates and ways of working that simplify the entire software development lifecycle. Today, we support more than 20 teams across all three divisions, combining hands-on engineering with coaching, training and technical enablement.

Ultimately, our goal is simple: remove complexity, create great developer experiences and enable teams to deliver secure, high-quality software faster.

Role Description
CORE Platform gives our DevOps teams a paved road to build, test, deploy and observe software safely and efficiently. Within Observability, we give teams the tools and capabilities they need to understand how their applications behave in production, identify problems and continuously improve.

As a Platform Engineer, you will design, build and evolve our shared observability capabilities, with a strong focus on reliability, security and performance. Our current landscape includes OpenTelemetry, OpenSearch Serverless, AWS services such as CloudWatch and X-Ray, and Datadog, but our tooling will continue to evolve. You will have the opportunity to evaluate new technologies and influence what we adopt next.

We work close to our DevOps teams and believe in starting small, learning fast and adjusting as we go. By understanding their challenges first-hand, you will help turn recurring needs into scalable, self-service solutions and golden paths that reduce complexity for teams across the organization.

Looking ahead, we are also preparing for AI agents to become platform users alongside developers. You will help shape how we make their behaviour observable, secure and understandable as they become part of the software development landscape. What you will do:
Design, build and operate observability capabilities with reliability, security and performance in focus.
Work with OpenTelemetry, OpenSearch, AWS native services and Datadog to create a consistent observability experience.
Collaborate closely with DevOps teams to understand their needs and solve real-world challenges.
Explore new ideas through proofs of concept and prototypes, learning and adjusting quickly.
Turn recurring needs into reusable, self-service golden paths, templates and documentation.
Support teams through troubleshooting, technical guidance and knowledge sharing.
Evaluate emerging observability technologies and help decide what we adopt, evolve or retire.

Your profile
Beyond your technical expertise, you are curious, collaborative and comfortable working close to the teams you support. You enjoy understanding challenges first-hand, experimenting with solutions and turning what works into something others can easily adopt and reuse.
 
You are comfortable navigating areas where there may not yet be an established best practice and bring clarity and structure along the way. You communicate openly, share your knowledge and care about creating solutions that make a real difference for developers.
 
You are also curious about the opportunities AI brings to software development, while taking a pragmatic view of where it creates real value. Most importantly, you are a humble team player with a positive attitude, a sense of humour and a genuine interest in succeeding together. We believe you bring:
